hygiene.**`), its own leading `**Draft-PR ensure` heading would have

## Replay evidence (orchestrator, 2026-08-20)

Mirrored `scripts/workflow_lint.py:13280-13296` exactly
(`idx = find("**Pre-split completeness guard")`;
`nxt = find("\n\n**", idx+1)`; `region = text[idx:nxt]`; require
`pre_split_review_guard.py` / `PRE-SPLIT-INCOMPLETE` / `remaining:`)
against the live `09-step-5.md` under three placements:

| Placement | region_len | tokens missing | live-tree test |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. live (no insert) | 1443 | none | PASS |
| B. chosen slot (after Round push hygiene) | 1443 | none | PASS |
| C. "forbidden" slot (before Round push hygiene) | 1443 | none | PASS |

`live == chosen == early` all True — the region is BYTE-IDENTICAL under
every placement considered.

Mechanism of the error: the "one position earlier" slot IS the region's
existing terminator position. The region already ends at the `\n\n`
preceding line 38, so whatever paragraph opens there becomes the
terminator. Inserting the ensure heading there merely REPLACES
`**Round push hygiene.**` as the terminator at the SAME byte offset;
nothing is truncated. The original reasoning conflated "becomes the
terminator" with "truncates the region" — those are only the same thing
if the insert lands strictly INSIDE the region.

## The risk is weaker still (control case, orchestrator addition)

Control D inserted the block strictly INSIDE the region (between the
guard paragraph and the ensemble paragraph). The region DID truncate
(1443 -> 1066 chars) — but all three required tokens SURVIVED and the
test would still PASS, because the tokens live at lines 18-28, inside
the first 1,066 chars.

So the honest statement is stronger than "the chosen slot is safe": the
predicate is insensitive to every placement at or after the guard
paragraph's end. Breaking it would require an insert strictly between
the guard heading (line 14) and the last required token (line 28) —
i.e. inside the guard's own prose block, which no reasonable edit would
do.

## Codex Must-Fix 1 (CONFIRMED): the infra retry path does not exist

Plan v3 claims the infra-path round-1 create failure is carried by "the
retry-while-unconfirmed arm + the between-round Round-push-hygiene
pushes". Both halves fail:

(a) **Round push hygiene does not mandate a push.** Verbatim
(`09-step-5.md:38-43`): "Any branch push run during this loop — yours
between rounds, or the implementer's per its spec — is BARE with its
exit code checked". That constrains the FORM of pushes that occur; it
never requires one to occur. Confirming grep: line 40 is the ONLY
push mention in the whole 103,751 B Step 5 file
(`grep -nE "push origin issue|push -u|MUST push|must push"` -> 1 hit).

(b) **A first-round PASS exits Step 5 immediately, so there is no "next
round entry" to retry at.** Verbatim (`09-step-5.md` § 5d): on
`final_verdict == PASS`, `infra` / `batch` / `analysis` / `survey` ->
"skip pod phase, move status directly to `reviewing`". The state
machine agrees (`SKILL.md:238-247`): only a FAIL re-enters the
implementing sub-phase.

Composed with the fact-checker's A7 correction (`implementer.md`
mandates COMMIT but no unconditional push before `epm:results`), the
realized failure path is:

  kind: infra  +  branch never pushed  +  round-1 review PASS
    -> ensure's create fails rc!=0 (branch absent from origin)
    -> NO retry (no round 2 exists)
    -> branch reaches Step 10d with zero PRs
    -> [step10d-no-pr-anomaly] fires

That is EXACTLY the outcome #2241 exists to eliminate, on a path the
plan itself labels normal — so acceptance criteria 1 and 2 are violated
for the single-round infra class, not merely "degraded to status quo".
Note the self-reference: #2241 is itself `kind: infra`.

Frequency judgement (for the reconciler / planner): the methodology
critic observed that infra pushes "often land anyway" in practice, and a
first-round PASS is common for small infra diffs — so this is a
plausible RECURRING path, not a corner case. The design's own fail-open
retry is what was supposed to cover it, and it cannot.

## Codex Must-Fix 2 (partially confirmed): latency claim vs the timeouts

The plan asserts "no probe or create failure may block, delay, or fail
the round" while its own sequential fences allow 75 s (probe) + 150 s
(create). Codex additionally found an INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY: §0
summarizes the worst case as "<= 75 s per round" while §9 states
"<= 75 s ... + 150 s". Both cannot be right.

Orchestrator adjudication of the related cross-lens split: the Claude
methodology critic argued the arms are mutually exclusive (a timed-out

SUCCESSFUL probe (up to ~75 s, rc=0) followed by a timing-out create

("correctly summed") are right; methodology's concern 3 is not.
Whether ~225 s bounded is an acceptable hot-path cost is a judgement
call, but the plan's ABSOLUTE "may not delay" phrasing is falsified by
its own fences and its two worst-case figures must be reconciled to one.
